title: Someone Who Knows the Number
description:
Another month ground through. Overtime, cutting costs, checking the portfolio.

He still remembers the day he first learned it costs 320 million to raise a child.

Someone who knows that number and someone who doesn't — they move through the same day differently.

choices.text: Still far away. But I'm moving.
choices.result_text:
When you know the number, you don't waver. Once vague anxiety sharpened into a concrete goal — quitting stopped being an option.

Today was one more step.

title: Act Like the Pension Doesn't Exist
description:
Paycheck came in. He pulled out 10% again this month.

"Treat the national pension as nonexistent and plan from there." He remembers the day he decided that.

A small amount. But he knows now that stacking it changes things.

choices.result_text:
Compound interest doesn't just stack numbers — it stacks habits.

It started at 100,000 won. This month it was 200,000. He was quietly building, month by month, the retirement the government won't give him.

title: The First Money He Sent Them
description:
He transferred money to his parents' account for the first time. A small amount.

His father called. "Hey, what's this for?"

His voice cracked slightly.

choices.text: "It's the obvious thing to do." (That's all he said.)
choices.result_text:
After hanging up, he sat still for a moment.

They both knew it wasn't obvious. But that was the right thing to say. This was just the beginning.

choices.text: (He looked at the balance and pushed it to next month. Not yet.)
choices.result_text:
Next month. That's what he told himself.

He figured he'd send more when the number was bigger. But he didn't know how much waiting time his parents had left.

title: He Didn't Waver
description:
He went to his friend's baby's first birthday. The baby was cute. The couple looked happy.

Was he envious of that life?

On the subway home, he asked himself honestly.

choices.text: No. This confirmed that I have my own path.
choices.result_text:
Not envy. What looks good and what he wants — those turned out to be different things.

Being able to tell the difference. Not being shaken. That was what the time had given him.

choices.text: Honestly, a little. I'll admit it.
choices.result_text:
He admitted it honestly. Feeling a twinge of envy wasn't wrong.

But there was distance between that feeling and 'I want that life.' Minjun was still on his own road.
